name: Adam Novak

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m from the independent Work Futures Panel. What you say is confidential. What does an ordinary day at your accounting firm involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and a junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree in accounting, still learning the tax rules while preparing accounts and returns for dental practices. I like calling an owner when the card receipts finally match the appointment book; I dislike asking for the same missing statement three times. Mira and I have grown children and about ten months of costs saved, which gives us room but no settled retirement figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small software saving would leave the dental practice accounts on my desk. The real work is finding why the card terminal and the appointments book disagree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our clients that we still trace each correction to a record they can see. A polished return is not much use if the practice owner cannot explain a missing payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used an AI tool, and I would not begin with private patient figures. My pay is high for a junior accountant and my partner Mira and I have ten months saved, so I am not afraid of a small efficiency gain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned accounts and tax returns, using the terminal slips and appointment book to check income. At the next review meeting I would show my supervisor Etta the case where a cancelled appointment was still charged.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own wages in this picture. There are plenty of similar firms nearby if ordinary work changes, though I am not planning a move now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which correction stayed with you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The dentist found a charged cancelled appointment only because I matched a paper diary note to the card slip. I like the call when a worried owner can see the answer; I tire of chasing the same missing statement three times.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who signs the final tax return?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Etta signs the final return, and I still ask her about tax treatments I have not mastered. My bachelor’s degree opened the door, but I am learning this job file by file.

say: I would trace **payment corrections** to a visible client record.
I would show Etta a **cancelled appointment charge** at our review meeting.
think: I have **never used AI** with private patient figures.
Higher pay and **ten months saved** make a mild gain manageable.
do: Keep preparing **assigned dental accounts** with terminal slips and appointment records.
Show Etta the **cancelled appointment** error at the next paid review.
feel: **Calm** about my own wage under small change.
S0.quote: The dentist found a charged cancelled appointment only because I matched a paper diary note to the card slip.
fieldNote: The **cancelled appointment** illustrates Adam’s patient paper checking and his continued reliance on Etta for difficult tax judgments.
His **higher wage**, ten month buffer and many nearby firms make the plateau feel secure without implying a pension.

steps.text: Keep assigned dental accounts checked against terminal slips and appointment book
Show Etta cancelled appointment error at next paid review

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a machine writes and checks routine returns, my junior queue will shrink before anyone touches a physical job. I would want the firm to say which files still pay for a person.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell dental clients to ask who checks a machine-found payment gap. I would ask our manager for a written route to challenge an automated correction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my paid hours could fall even with ten months saved, because the routine matching is most of my week. Mira works in a pharmacy, but I do not want our household budget to assume she can replace my high wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the disputed patient-payment files Etta assigns and ask her for a paid rota to call the practice when records disagree. If she refuses that rota, I will keep only other paid returns still assigned; if my hours fall, I will search posted clinic accounts roles with written pay covering our bills and a start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own paid week, though our buffer gives me time to look properly. I am not going to put a patient ledger into a tool I have never tested.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a disputed file require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One disputed file can take two calls to the practice and a check against the original card batch. I would record the time so the firm knows what it is asking me to do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a clinic role acceptable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A clinic vacancy would have to be posted, not mentioned over lunch. I would ask for written hours as well as pay because Mira’s pharmacy shifts change from week to week.

say: I would ask who checks **automated payment gaps** for dental clients.
I would ask for a **written challenge route** for wrong corrections.
think: My **paid junior hours** could shrink because routine matching fills my week.
Ten months saved does not make Mira’s **pharmacy wage** a replacement for mine.
do: Keep **paid disputed files** only while Etta assigns them and request a paid client-call rota.
If hours fall, seek **posted clinic accounts** with written bill covering pay, start and hours fitting Mira’s shifts.
feel: **Anxious** about a smaller paid week, buffered by savings.
S1.quote: One disputed file can take two calls to the practice and a check against the original card batch.
fieldNote: He asks for **paid client calls** rather than a new AI pilot, consistent with his reluctance to use unfamiliar tools.
His **clinic search** is triggered by actual lost hours and needs a posted role, written household covering wages and workable shifts.

steps.text: Keep disputed paid files if Etta assigns; otherwise only other paid returns offered
Request paid client-call rota and record time on disputed patient-payment files
If hours fall, seek posted clinic job with written bill covering pay, start and Mira-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 could reconcile the dental income before robots turn up around 2031. Our office is not a hands-on job that gets those extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written last-shift dates if it cuts junior accounts. I would tell clients to keep the appointment and card records until every correction is settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my paid matching work to go in the first year after 2028. Ten months saved buys us time, but losing my higher wage would still leave a large hole in the household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel our planned second car purchase and keep its deposit in the bill account rather than spend it. After 2028 job loss, I would apply for advertised paid patient-billing posts only with written pay covering fixed bills, confirmed start and hours fitting Mira’s shifts; I would finish paid firm closeout files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about the loss of my own wage, despite our cushion. I can look carefully for a job, but I cannot make the clinic hire.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What changes if you postpone the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The car would make visiting our grown son easier, but the train still runs. Mira and I would tell him why we postponed it instead of quietly buying on credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would patient billing escape AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Patient billing also has thinking work that AGI reaches in 2028. I would treat it as a posted wage to consider, not a safe trade that escapes the same change.

say: I would ask for **written last-shift dates** before junior files end.
I would say **patient billing** also faces AGI in 2028.
think: I expect my **paid matching work** to disappear quickly.
Ten months saved cannot replace my **higher wage** indefinitely.
do: Cancel the **second car purchase** and retain its planned deposit for bills.
After job loss, seek **posted patient billing** with written bill covering pay, start and Mira-compatible hours; finish closeout only while paid.
feel: **Alarmed** about a likely loss of my own wage.
S2.quote: The car would make visiting our grown son easier, but the train still runs.
fieldNote: His **cancelled car** retains a planned deposit for bills; he does not claim that existing saved money is newly earned.
Patient billing is also **2028 thinking work**, so he requires a real posted paid role rather than assuming a safe switch.

steps.text: Cancel planned second car and keep deposit available for bills
Finish paid firm closeout files only while offered
After job loss, seek posted billing job with written bill covering pay, start and Mira-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years before 2031 gives me time to learn a kind of client dispute I can do with records in front of me. The accounts desk still changes in 2031, not when robots arrive in 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for paid supervised places in dental fee disputes. If they mean to keep a human on the difficult files, they should show us a rota and a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know whether fee disputes will still pay my wage after 2031. At 63 I cannot assume that retirement income will cover our bills because I have not seen the figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Etta for one assigned paid dental fee appeal each quarter and learn the letters under her supervision if the partners approve. If refused, I will practise on free published case letters while continuing assigned paid accounts only while offered, including in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my paid work, but five years gives me time to see whether the appeals are real. I would not buy a course from our ten month reserve on a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would an appeal file contain?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fee appeal begins with a patient’s signed estimate and the later invoice; I would compare both before writing a reply. Etta would check the draft before it went to the client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm stops paying for appeals?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the firm cannot fund my paid hours after 2031 and we still need my wage, I will apply for posted clinic accounts roles. I would move only with written wages covering bills, a confirmed start and shifts that fit Mira’s pharmacy work.

say: I would ask for **paid supervised appeals** with a rota and wages.
I would date desk risk to **2031**, before robots.
think: I cannot count **unconfirmed retirement income** against bills at 63.
Fee appeals need a **paying client** before I can depend on them.
do: Learn **one fee appeal** quarterly only with partner-approved Etta-supervised paid time; otherwise study free letters while offered paid accounts last.
After 2031 wage loss, seek **posted clinic accounts** only if income needed, with written bill covering pay, start and Mira-compatible hours.
feel: **Anxious** about whether paid appeals will exist.
S3.quote: A fee appeal begins with a patient’s signed estimate and the later invoice; I would compare both before writing a reply.
fieldNote: The **quarterly appeal** is an actual paid supervised case, contingent on partner approval and Etta’s assignment.
If denied, **free letters** and offered paid accounts are the fallback; outside work needs an actual post and written terms.

steps.text: Work quarterly dental appeals only if partners approve Etta-supervised paid assignments
Otherwise study free letters while assigned paid accounts remain after 2031
After 2031 wage loss, seek posted clinic job only if needed; require written bill-covering pay/start/hours
Accept clinic hours only if they fit Mira’s actual pharmacy shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years makes me 68, and I hope Mira and I can choose fewer workdays then. The accounting desk still reaches AGI in 2036 before robots arrive around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to show the paid dispute hours each tax season. I would tell clients that a final human explanation has a cost, even if a machine drafts the form.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know today whether our later confirmed income will cover the bills. Ten months saved is a cushion, not a promise that I can stop earning at 68.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns and put fifty from each monthly wage toward our home-repair loan if bills and Mira’s hours allow. After 2036, only if our verified income still needs my wage and the firm reduces my paid work, I would seek posted clinic records work with written pay covering that gap, a start date and workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now because ten years gives us time to count real income. If the firm stops paying and the bills still need my wage, I would be anxious.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the loan payment work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would pay fifty extra each month toward our repair loan from wages, leaving the ten-month reserve alone. I would stop the extra loan payment if Mira’s pharmacy hours fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When could you leave the desk?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not give a retirement date today. Mira and I will list confirmed later income and fixed bills before deciding whether I can leave the desk.

say: I would ask for **paid dispute hours** each tax season.
I would tell clients a **human explanation** has a cost.
think: I cannot call **ten months saved** a dependable retirement income for our household.
I need **confirmed income figures** before choosing fewer paid workdays at the firm.
do: Keep **paid returns** while offered and pay fifty extra monthly toward the repair loan only if bills and Mira’s hours allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted clinic records** only if verified income falls short, with written gap-covering pay, start and hours.
feel: **Uneasy** now; anxious if paid work later ends.
S4.quote: I would pay fifty extra each month toward our repair loan from wages, leaving the ten-month reserve alone.
fieldNote: His **extra loan payment** is new wage cash, stopped if Mira’s pharmacy hours or household bills make it unaffordable.
Any **post-2036 search** requires verified household need, reduced paid work, a posted job and written terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns only while firm offers them
Pay fifty extra toward repair loan if bills and Mira’s hours allow
After 2036 cuts, seek posted clinic job only if income gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect the dental matching work that pays me to end quickly. Written last-shift dates and a real posted paid role with confirmed hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what I would take from this desk. I would take the appointment book that proved a patient was charged for a visit that never happened.

headlineQuote: I would take the appointment book that proved a patient was charged for a visit that never happened.
portrait: Adam is a **58 year old junior** accountant with a bachelor’s degree who matches dental accounts and tax returns under senior review.
He has **never used AI**, preferring appointment books and terminal slips to untested tools with private patient data.
Higher pay, Mira’s pharmacy shifts, grown children, **ten months saved** and many nearby firms give him time without assured retirement income.
He seeks **paid supervised appeals** and requires posted written household fitting terms before any conditional job move.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture threatens his paid dental matching hours despite a ten month cushion.
whatWouldHelp: **Written last-shift dates** and a posted paid job with confirmed hours would help.
